transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I just can’t stop fixating on how bad I look in every picture, and it’s starting to really interfere with my work and social life. It has gotten to the point where it's hard to focus on anything else, and I just feel incredibly overwhelmed.
When you look at these pictures, is there a specific feature or part of your appearance that you feel is flawed or misshapen, even if others tell you it looks fine?

Yes, I'm completely fixated on my nose and my skin. Whenever I see a photo, all I can see is how huge and crooked my nose looks and how uneven my skin is. I end up zooming in and picking those areas apart for hours, even though everyone tells me I look totally fine.

When you feel anxious in social situations or avoid them, is it mainly because you worry people will notice and judge your nose or skin, or is it a more general fear of being embarrassed or scrutinized?

It is definitely about my nose and skin specifically, rather than a general fear of social situations. I am just terrified that people will notice how crooked my nose is and how uneven my skin looks, which is why I try so hard to hide them with makeup and avoid being on camera. I just can't stand the thought of anyone seeing those flaws.

Aside from these concerns about your appearance, do you experience other repetitive thoughts or behaviors, such as a need to constantly check things, fears of germs, or needing items to be arranged in a specific way?

No, I don't really have those kinds of thoughts or behaviors, like worrying about germs or needing to arrange things. All of my focus and the repetitive things I do are really just about my appearance and trying to fix how I look in photos.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a profound preoccupation with imagined or minor defects in their physical appearance, specifically focusing on their nose (perceived as huge and crooked) and skin (perceived as uneven). These perceived flaws are not noticeable to others. The preoccupation leads to repetitive, time-consuming behaviors (zooming in and analyzing photos for hours, heavy makeup use to camouflage) and significant avoidance of social situations and cameras due to fear of judgment. This clinical picture is diagnostic of Body Dysmorphic Disorder, which is classified under F45.2 (Hypochondriacal disorder) in ICD-10.
